EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows classic para-disubstituted benzene features: a very intense band at ~831 cm⁻¹ with a companion near 816 cm⁻¹ (characteristic out-of-plane C–H modes), a strong ring/CH-in-plane band at ~1208 cm⁻¹, and aromatic C–H stretches at 3022–3064 cm⁻¹ together with aliphatic CH₃ stretches at 2872–2929 cm⁻¹ (consistent with GFQ-003). The CH₃ deformation at 1382 cm⁻¹ is relatively strong while the 1451 cm⁻¹ band is weak, fitting two methyl substituents rather than an ethyl group (which would give a stronger CH₂ scissor near 1450). No C=O, O–H, or N=N-specific bands are evident, excluding amide/phenol/diazene candidates. These features best match p‑xylene (candidate 1).
